# The three reviewed waivers that carried PR #392 (the elps v1.48.1 -> v1.50.0
# bump) while main's cached benchmark baseline still predated the merge. They
# were retired from scripts/benchstat-waivers.txt once the baseline caught up
# and the gate reported all three as waiver-unused; they live on here as the
# round-trip fixture proving the waiver mechanism end-to-end against the real
# comparison from that PR (benchstat-waived-regression-392.txt).
github.com/luthersystems/substrate/internal/substrate/shirocore | Utils/$load | B/op | 20 | 2027-02-28 | substrate#392 elps#442 | elps v1.48.1 -> v1.50.0 aliasing fixes (elps#442, #467, #496, #419) allocate more while resolving and recording symbol aliases during load. 10.81Mi -> 12.74Mi (+17.82%, p=0.008 n=5) on the core-library load, paid ONCE per environment rather than per call; sec/op on this row IMPROVED and is still gated at full strength. The alternative was staying on v1.48.1 with the aliasing bugs. Ceiling 20% against a measured 17.82%, so a second regression landing on this row still reds the build.
github.com/luthersystems/substrate/internal/substrate/shirocore | Utils/$load | allocs/op | 14 | 2027-02-28 | substrate#392 elps#442 | The same load-path allocations as the B/op waiver above, counted instead of weighed: +11.50% (p=0.008 n=5). One cost measured two ways, so waiving one column and not the other would not be narrower, only broken -- the build would stay red on a row nobody had reviewed. Same bump, same tracking issue, same expiry. Ceiling 14% against a measured 11.50%.
github.com/luthersystems/substrate/internal/substrate/shiro/preheat | PhylumPreheater_initPhylum | B/op | 15 | 2027-02-28 | substrate#392 elps#419 | The same elps v1.50.0 aliasing work seen from the preheater: building a preheated phylum environment allocates +12.85% (p=0.008 n=5) more bytes, once per environment, because the alias tables are populated while the phylum is initialised. This benchmark's allocs/op moved by less than the gate and is deliberately NOT waived, and its sec/op improved. Ceiling 15% against a measured 12.85%.
